sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's accelerating data-center buildout and government digitalization push create durable demand for local connectivity and infrastructure providers like INET and IRSX.
Domestic tech names are decoupling from US-listed peers, driven by rupiah-stable earnings and rising institutional allocation to IDX-listed growth stories.
Consolidation in Indonesia's telecom and tower space favors scaled players like YELO and WIFI, as spectrum and infrastructure costs push smaller rivals out.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in INET and YELO on domestic data-center and connectivity demand; trim US-exposed names like WIFI into strength as Nasdaq weakness persists. Rotate toward ID-listed tech with local revenue visibility, prioritizing IRSX and CENT for infrastructure-linked upside. Maintain WATCH signal; add only on confirmed IDX tech breadth expansion above 50-day averages.

Sector breadth is neutral, so avoid chasing INDO and 2881 after sharp moves; add on 2-3% dips. US financials' mild strength supports sentiment, yet local catalysts remain stock-specific. Trim any laggards to recycle into leaders.

Climate-tech divergence between ID and US signals capital rotation toward emerging-market energy transition assets, driven by lower valuations and faster policy execution in Indonesia's 2060 net-zero
sectors.ai: Buy BATR and POWR on relative strength; trim EIX into strength. US renewables lag on rates, but Indonesia's green capex and captive demand underpin upside. Rotate into utilities with regulated cash flows (SRE, AWK) for defensive exposure. Watch for policy catalysts from Indonesia's RUPTL revision; add on dips below -1% aggregate.

sectors.ai: Buy selective small-cap consumer names showing volume-driven re-rating (PADA, JARR, PGUN) as domestic demand stabilizes, but avoid chasing BEEF/AGAR momentum without earnings confirmation. sectors.name: Infrastructure
themes: Indonesia's accelerated national strategic project (PSN) pipeline, including toll roads and ports, is a durable demand driver for contractors like KIJA and YPAS through 2025-2026.
Telecom tower and data-center infrastructure (TOWR, PACK) benefits from structural digital adoption and 5G rollout, with recurring lease revenue insulating against construction cyclicality.
Domestic infrastructure outperformance vs US (-1.28%) reflects local monetary easing expectations and fiscal stimulus, favoring IDX-listed operators over global-linked peers in a rate-cut cycle.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian infrastructure names with confirmed order books (KIJA, TOWR) and avoid chasing speculative penny movers (ASLI, TEBE) lacking earnings support. The sector's aggregate gain masks divergence—domestic strength (+1.73%) vs US drag (-1.28%) favors local toll, tower, and data-center plays. Accumulate on dips toward 0.39% aggregate, targeting KIJA and TOWR for 3-6 month upside as government capex accelerates ahead of 2025 elections.

sectors.name: Healthcare
themes: Indonesia's hospital operators (RSGK, LABS) are consolidating mid-tier facilities, driving durable same-store revenue growth as private insurance penetration rises.
Global plasma-derived therapies (CSL) face a multi-year supply-demand gap, underpinning pricing power and margin expansion beyond cyclical recovery.
Obesity and metabolic drug pipelines (LLY, PODD) are shifting care delivery toward chronic disease management, creating durable demand for delivery devices and companion diagnostics.
sectors.ai: Healthcare's aggregate uptick is broad-based, not idiosyncratic, with global large-caps (LLY, ABBV, JNJ) and Indonesia's RSGK/LABS confirming a risk-on rotation into defensive growth. Buy pullbacks in CSL (plasma pricing power) and RSGK (domestic hospital consolidation), but trim PODD after its 5.96% pop—valuation is stretched. Position for sustained M&A and GLP-1 spillover into diagnostics and distribution.

US weakness is a headwind for global names, so overweight ID-centric operators. Add RMKE for coal haulage tailwind; trim TAXI on speculative froth. Position for Q3 volume data and tariff-driven rerating.
